The Art of Watchmaking

Every second, engineered to perfection

Inside every Neil timepiece beats a movement designed, finished and regulated under one roof in Henley-on-Thames. Bridges are chamfered by hand, screws are heat-blued, and each calibre is regulated in five positions before it is cased.

No shortcuts. No bought-in anonymity. Just 214 components working in concert — visible through sapphire, exactly as a mechanical watch should be.

Our Story

Built on heritage. Designed for the future.

Neil was founded on a simple conviction — that Britain, the nation that gave the world marine chronometry, should once again make watches worth keeping. From a single workshop bench in Oxfordshire to an atelier on the Thames, every generation of Neil has been built by hand and built to last.

2002

The first bench. Neil is founded in a converted Oxfordshire coach house, restoring vintage British movements.

2009

The first collection. The Heritage line launches — 300 pieces, sold out within the year.

2016

Calibre H-01. Our first fully in-house movement, five years in development.

Today

The Wing, Henley. Design, engineering and assembly under one roof — every watch still finished by a single watchmaker.

“A watch should outlive its maker — and be worth handing down.”
